axis: keeping steady under stress → wholly untroubled evenness of temper

members.tone: The plain name for holding steady when pressure is on, with none of the flourish *aplomb* brings to the same feat.
Bare and short — names the steady state itself rather than the effort of keeping it, which is what *composure* implies.
The flat quality-noun, describing the steadiness rather than admiring it as *equanimity* does.
Elevated and admiring — steadiness under stress treated as an evenness of temper worth crediting, well above workaday *calmness*.
Praise with a flourish: the coolness under strain reads as polished and assured, not merely maintained.
Puts the weight on self-certainty as the root of the coolness, plainer and less stylish than *aplomb*.
Informal and offhand — makes great steadiness under strain sound like something a person simply has, and can lose, where *sang-froid* makes it formal.
Adds balance and bearing to the coolness, praising how the strain is carried as much as the nerve behind it.
Formal and faintly glamorous — nerve praised as a chill that strain cannot reach, more theatrical than *composure*.
The freedom from stress sounds like an ease rested in, warmer than the unstirred flatness of *placidity*.
The plainest of these: a temperament with no emotional weather in it, and none of the loftiness of *serenity*.
Even and unruffled, the absence of emotion sounding closer to a settled flatness than to any achievement.
Lofty and admiring — an untroubled disposition raised almost to a grace, far above bare *quiet*.
Soothing rather than exalted: the stressless disposition praised as restfulness, without *serenity*'s elevation.
The same restful freedom from stress and emotion as *tranquillity*, carried under the single-l spelling.
